````text
# #3712: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 43045496212](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43045496212) on `_staging` (`bd47844`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|

| [e2e (5/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43045496212/job/130613280964) | failure |
| [e2e (6/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43045496212/job/130613281020) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `_staging`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`, and you take it before every other queued item): production promotes itself only from a daily run on `_staging` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix, and `_staging` holds still until this issue closes (scripts/promote-staging.sh, the freeze). Fix every failed job here, in the one pull request on `main` that closes this: when it closes, `_staging` takes main's first green commit after the close and the super run starts on it at once, and a run still red opens a new issue. Before you start, look for an open pull request or issue already fixing one of these jobs, and build on it instead of fixing the same test twice. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43057110849)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

This plan makes two of the four failed jobs pass: `fuzz (1/4)` and `e2e (5/8)`. The other two need a person:

- **`e2e component (chrome)`** stays red. The spec that fails is `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx`, and two earlier bot issues already work on it (#3633, then #3674 with PR #3691, now in the merge queue). Its builder found that the Mythic takeover still misses its budget after #3691, and stopped asking a person to open a follow-up issue.
- **`e2e (6/8)`** did not fail here. All seven of its specs pass on this runner, so only the job's log can say what broke.

Both are under **Open questions**.

## Goal

1. **`fuzz (1/4)`.** The serialized-restart check's clock times only the restart itself: the state's JSON round trip and its two hashes. The continuation after it (the rest of the game replayed through `reduce`) is still checked against the live hash and ending, but no longer timed.
2. **`e2e (5/8)`.** Spec 50's idle window stops counting the work Cypress's own command log does on the page's main thread.
3. **The pull request description** says which job each fix makes pass and how it was checked. It also says `e2e component (chrome)` and `e2e (6/8)` are not fixed here, and why.

**What was found** (on `main` at f803f1b, on a 4-core runner like CI's, Chrome 156, `CI=true`):

- **fuzz.**
  - `fuzz --from 1 --seeds 2500` fails seed 247 only, in the checkpoint stage: "checkpoint took 8106ms, past CHECKPOINT_TIME_BOUND_MS (5000ms)".
  - An instrumented copy shows the round trip takes 2 ms. The continuation takes 3.4 s, and one action is 3.0–3.6 s of it: `play classicplus-047` (Jogg's Box, about 26 random casts).
  - Inside that action, a single random cast of core-097 (Zephrys) takes 3.8–4.4 s. That is the §10.7 scorer in `crates/engine/src/subsystems/scorer.rs`: about 600 candidates, up to 8 trial copies each, on a board of about 300 instances. Every other cast takes 3.4 ms or less.
  - The bound was written for "pathological serialization blowup" (#1387). #1803 already took the prefix fold out of the clock because its cost grows with the game; the continuation's cost grows the same way.
  - The handicapped wave passed, but its slowest checkpoint was 4246 ms of the 5000 ms bound.
- **Spec 50.**
  - The idle phase fails on a quiet machine: 11 and then 7 long tasks against `FRAME_LONG_TASK_BUDGET_IDLE` (5). Its p95 frame time is well within budget.
  - The cause is the client's voice prefetch (`apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` `schedulePrefetch`, 1465 files). It fetches about 100 files during the window, and Cypress logs each one as a command-log row. Re-rendering and scrolling that log runs on the page's main thread; a CPU profile shows `_isFullyVisible` taking 1.7 s of the 5 s window.
  - With `cy.intercept({ url: "**/audio/**" }, { log: false })` the files still load (7866 bytes either way) and the window shows 0 long tasks of the app's own.
  - A copy of spec 50 with the intercept passed 3 of 3 tests, twice: idle median 16.7 ms, p95 33 ms, 1 long task.

     /// How long the planted continuation sleeps before its first action: far over seed 1's round
     /// trip, so a clock that still counted the continuation would report at least this much.
     const PLANTED_CONTINUATION_MS: u64 = 300;
     thread_local! {
         /// Whether the planted continuation has slept yet on this thread.
         static PLANTED_SLEPT: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
     }
     /// `reduce`, after sleeping PLANTED_CONTINUATION_MS before the first action on this thread.
     fn slow_continuation(state: &GameState, action: &Action) -> ReduceResult {
         if !PLANTED_SLEPT.with(|slept| slept.replace(true)) {
             std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(PLANTED_CONTINUATION_MS));
         }
         reduce(state, action)
     }
     /// #3712: the bound times the restart, the round trip and its hashes, never the continuation's
     /// own `reduce`: one planted slow still passes, and the report carries the round trip's cost.
     #[test]
     fn the_checkpoint_clock_times_the_round_trip_and_not_the_continuation() {
         let _preview = preview_every_set();
         let run = seed_one();
         let setup = GameSetup::gate(1);
         let (step, _) = checkpoint_step(&setup.stream("checkpoint-"), &run.paused, run.log.len());
         assert!(step < run.log.len(), "seed 1's checkpoint at {step} of {} leaves nothing to continue", run.log.len());
         PLANTED_SLEPT.with(|slept| slept.set(false));
         let report = check_serial_restart_with(&setup, &run.decks, &run.log, &run.state, &run.paused, slow_continuation)
             .unwrap_or_else(|failure| panic!("{}", failure.message));
         assert!(PLANTED_SLEPT.with(Cell::get), "the continuation went through the planted reducer");
         assert!(report.ms < u128::from(PLANTED_CONTINUATION_MS), "the checkpoint's clock counted the continuation: {}ms", report.ms);
     }
     ```
5. **`crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs`, `check_duos_serial_restart` (about line 676).**
   - Same split: the wrapper calls `check_duos_serial_restart_with(options, log, live, stream, paused, duos_reduce)`.
   - The new function takes `continue_with: DuosReducer` and has the doc "`check_duos_serial_restart`, the rest of the log applied through `continue_with` (`duos_reduce`; a test plants a slow one, #3712)."
   - In the body, after `verify_round_trip(…)?;`, insert:

     // #3712: the restart's cost ends here; the continuation is the game's own, checked but not timed.

     - It asserts `step < run.log.len()`, that the flag was set, and `ms < u128::from(PLANTED_CONTINUATION_MS)`.
7. Run `cargo fmt`.
8. **`e2e/cypress/e2e/50-busy-board-frames.cy.ts`.**

## Tests

Before testing, note that `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` may be set (it is on the bots' runners). Use `${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}/release/jackioh`. Spec 01's replay task wants `target/release/jackioh` in the worktree; if you link it there, remove the link before you stop.

- **The fix's own tests.** `cargo test -p jackioh-tools the_checkpoint_clock_times_the_round_trip_and_not_the_continuation` runs both new tests.
  - With step 2's or step 5's clock moved back, they fail at 345 ms and 535 ms; with the fix, both pass.
  - Then run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz_serial_restart` and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools duos_checkpoint_stage`: all 11 must pass.
- **The fuzz job.** Run `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools`, then `"$J" fuzz --from 247 --seeds 1`; it must pass with "slowest 1ms" or similar.
  - Then run fuzz shard 1's own commands: `"$J" fuzz --from 1 --seeds 2500`, `"$J" fuzz --from 1 --seeds 2500 --handicap` and `"$J" fuzz --duos --from 1 --seeds 500`. Each takes about 10 minutes with the shell's timeout raised, and each must report 0 failed.
- **Spec 50.** Run `pnpm --dir e2e probe:frames`. Or by hand:
  - `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm --dir apps/web build:e2e`, then serve it with `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vite preview --port 5173 --strictPort`.
  - Then `cd e2e && CI=true E2E=1 pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec cypress/e2e/50-busy-board-frames.cy.ts`.
  - All 3 tests must pass, with idle long tasks at 1 or fewer.
  - Never leave a temporary spec in `e2e/cypress/e2e/`: `shard-specs.mjs` would shift the shards.
- **Lint and types.** `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint e2e`, and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Done when

- [ ] Steps 1–9 are in, and the builder made no change elsewhere.
- [ ] Both new tests pass, and the 11 checkpoint tests pass.
- [ ] Seed 247 and shard 1's three waves report 0 failed.
- [ ] Spec 50 passes 3 of 3.
- [ ] e2e typecheck, eslint, fmt and clippy pass, and the harness's checks pass.
- [ ] The pull request body is as in step 10.

## Risks

- **A restored game that plays slower than the live one is no longer timed.** Its hash and ending are still checked, `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS` still stops a runaway seed, and `cargo jackioh perf` still holds `reduce` to its budgets. The rejected alternatives were raising the bound (a raised timeout) and speeding up the scorer (an engine change whose results must stay bit-identical for replay).
- **Determinism and replay.** No engine, card or client code changes, so no hash or golden replay moves.
- **The intercept.** With only `log`, Cypress passes the request through: the bytes were checked equal. It is scoped to spec 50. A global hook in `e2e/support/e2e.ts` was rejected because spec 01 only went from 70 s to 66.7 s, so nothing shows other specs need it.
- **The new tests' timing.** Seed 1's round trip in a debug build stayed far below 300 ms (both tests passed).

## Open questions

1. **`e2e component (chrome)`.** It stays red after this pull request. `fx-phone-living-game`'s Mythic takeover takes 153–224 ms on its worst frame against `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` (120 ms), and up to 55 ms mean against 50 ms, under 4x CPU throttling on a quiet runner.
   - #3633 and #3674 (PR #3691) are already working on it. #3674's last run found the takeover still misses, the cost being the board's React commits.
   - It also found that the broadside's retry never re-animates, which hides the four moments after it.
   - A person opens the follow-up issue #3674 asked for, or decides how R3351000's spec gates the daily run.
2. **`e2e (6/8)`.** All seven of its specs passed here. A person reads job 130613281020's log and posts which spec failed and its error on #3712.
3. **Closing #3712.** Merging this pull request closes #3712 (the harness writes "Closes") while those two jobs can stay red, so the next red run opens a new issue. A person accepts that or says how this pull request should land, as on #3674.
4. **Zephrys's cost.** One Zephrys dry run takes about 4 s on a 300-instance board. The server's match actor, and the browser in practice mode, would stall that long. Whether that warrants a performance issue is for a person to decide.
````
